subject.title: feat(workspace): add tiered bootstrap loading with configurable bootstrapTier

question: Should OpenClaw accept `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` as a core config surface now, with no-override behavior preserved and `full` as the only tier that includes `bootstrap-extra-files` hook extras?
rationale: The source gap is real and the implementation is bounded, but choosing this public config/default contract affects prompt context, session behavior, hook extras, docs, and overlapping bootstrap-control proposals.

options.title: Sponsor focused tier contract
options.body: Proceed with maintainer review of this PR as the additive config path, requiring unchanged no-override defaults plus docs/tests for resolver, hook, schema, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Fold into broader selector design
options.body: Pause this PR behind the broader deterministic bootstrap/context selector work so one public contract covers tiering, per-session filters, and related prompt-pressure issues.

options.title: Decline a new config knob
options.body: Keep fixed filters and steer users toward existing context controls such as `contextInjection`, bootstrap budgets, per-agent profiles, and heartbeat `lightContext`.

recommendation.title: Sponsor focused tier contract
recommendation.body: Proceed with maintainer review of this PR as the additive config path, requiring unchanged no-override defaults plus docs/tests for resolver, hook, schema, and upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the clearest combined signal from prior review context and adjacent bootstrap/config ownership.
